essential: The opening irony that America takes tragedy lightly: three political murders cast scarcely a shadow on the White House.

Hay's 1901 griefs in order, with Hay's own quoted voice: his son Del's death, McKinley's death, Nicolay dying, King dying. Keep Hay's lament for King, including 'best and brightest man of his generation' and 'Ca vous amuse, la vie?'.
Adams lands on December 29 to a summons to King's funeral. Roosevelt's accession makes the older men old and breaks the social ties among them.
The tone-flip of 'Ca vous amuse, la vie?' as Adams's own refrain. Hay is half glad to stay in office; for Adams it is pure loss.
Roosevelt aged 43 against the friends aged 63. 'Pure act' makes a teacher-pupil relation impossible. The Seneca/Nero parable and the moth keeping to the north side of La Fayette Square.
Power is poison: the President's excitement and reaction, and the 'wolves and hounds'. Roosevelt's honest intent but chronic excitement, offered as a measure of society's self-control.

Lodge is lost by the 'law of politics'. Include Massachusetts' incompatible standards (State Street, clergy, Harvard, the Irish, socialists). Include Lodge's shifting poses and the plumage-versus-crows image.
Adams shares the Boston double standard (theory of French measure, love of Shakespeare's 'conservative Christian anarchy') 'but he was not a Senator'. Double standards are fatal to politicians.
Domestic politics is men controlling dumb forces round power-houses. Foreign affairs, by contrast, give the only sure base for a chart of history.
The Secretary of State is as alone as the historian, against a hostile Senate. This makes Hay the best schoolmaster since 1865.

Hay's achievements: Britain won with six negative votes, France brought in via England, Germany next, Russia last. 'McKinleyism' is paradoxically the socialist scheme of Jaures and Bebel: a Coal-power combination against a Gun-power combination.
The final reversal: the height of knowledge reveals total ignorance. The Czar, the Kaiser and the Mikado knew nothing either.

essential: Summer 1902: the Inverlochy gloom and the flight back to Paris. Adams settles in Reynolds Hitt's attic 'in ignorance and silence'. A sentence or two will do.
Drift replaces effort. Lines of will become lines of force and then lines of attraction, so he enters the mechanical theory unknowingly. Credit this to the dynamo and the Virgin.
History of the motor: occult attraction before 1500, then vis a tergo. Pascal's ennui with one quotation. Ennui explains change but not its direction, so an outside attractive force is needed.

The imagined dialogue. The Virgin answers that she and Christ are Love and sends him to the schools. Aquinas says Love is one Force and the Schools give Multiplicity Form, Unity and Motive. Mark both clearly as imagined speech.
Abolishing man yields pantheism: God as continuous movement and interchangeable force. Aquinas looks more scientific than Haeckel or Mach because thought gives unity.
The dilemma of insisting on a universe drives one to the Church. There are two practical escapes, and the warning about the trap of logic.
The honest alternative is to deny unity, which would require a new education at sixty-five. Society would punish denial. Nihilism has no bottom; philosophers assume a bottom.
The kinetic theory of gases is science's final synthesis. Unity therefore equals multiplicity. Science offers only a 'larger synthesis'; the anarchist bomb forces him on.
The philosophers (Descartes through Hartmann) all affirm unity, and it reduces to psychology. Introspection is the most heart-rending tragedy.
The new psychology splits personality. The bicycle-rider and acrobat images show that normal thought is dispersion and sanity is artifice.
He is driven back on thought as one continuous Force, with the law that history needs a scale.
Man must be measured from a fixed point, 1150–1250 (Amiens, Aquinas). The two book titles as two points to project lines from. He sails home.
optional: The Lochaber, the 1879 harvest and the Switzerland/Carlsruhe itinerary can be reduced to a clause.

The second Pascal sentence can be cut if the first remains.

The list of the psychology institutions (Harvard, France, England) can be cut.
The dream and Welsh rarebit example can be cut.
risks: The argument is dense, so cutting intermediate steps may make the unity-equals-multiplicity turn abrupt.

essential: Washington's task of controlling planetary New York. The forces are aligned only in foreign affairs.
Hay at his summit on the edge of wreck over China's open door. Herbert succeeds Pauncefote, and friendship reduces friction.
The Kaiser recalls Holleben and sends Speck von Sternburg. Germany swings west, which isolates Cassini and leaves Hay's problem as Russia alone. Adams's admiration for this 'paradox'.

Russia as the enigma. Adams has personal reasons for goodwill (Alexander I and J. Q. Adams; Alexander II in 1862). His hope that Russia joins the combine within sixty years. Cassini's transparent emotion and Russia's fatal rolling.
Russia plus China forms one undeflectable mass. The insect's chart of spring 1903 shows the open door failing and the game seemingly lost. Present this as Adams's forecast then, not as fact.
The inertia questions: volume against intensity, vis nova against vis inertiae. His redefinition of mental inertia as movement round habitual motives.
Minds are unequally inert. Race-inertia is constant. Sex-inertia has never been overcome; maternity is the unbroken sequence; Americans ignore sex.
Early Women became a passion. The dinner-table trick and its answer. The May 1903 farewell dinner with the named guests, in which Adams's speech names each superior wife; the men laugh a little.
The clever woman's bitterness: the family dissolved, no place in Church or State, motherhood over at forty.

Artificial energy has been turned over to the American woman. She has been volatilized like a perfect gas, with millions of new working women. Can inertia take direction except along lines of inertia?
She follows the man, whose hand is on the lever. She becomes sexless and must marry machinery. Religion is the old refuge; the Church was a woman's protest.
The historian cannot take sides and can learn only from the birth-rate. Ironic proposals (census, Senate law). Faust is helpless. Ending: Russia seems easier than America; the horseshoe crab retreat.

essential: The voyage along Multiplicity has touched race and sex. Pumpelly says Willard Gibbs got help from Pearson's Grammar of Science. Adams reads it in Paris until December 26.

His mathematical ignorance denies him the right to judge. The Grammar seems an enlargement of Stallo but marks a historic English stride after twenty years of silence. Langley's Smithsonian papers (Crookes, Roentgen, Curie) prepared him.

Pearson's attack on Kelvin's textbooks and the deep-sea-fish circle of the senses. Include the Pearson quotes, attributed: order belongs to the mind, there is no inference beyond the senses, chaos. Keep Adams's crystal objection.

English thought forbids knowing the unknowable yet thinks about it. Everyone from Pythagoras to Hegel sailed into the supersensual calling it unity. Only the Church and Pearson agree. The Tennyson lines, briefly.
The change of 1900 was long prepared (1893, radium in 1898). The uniformitarians' contradictions were wrecked by rays. Science is adrift on a sensual raft, as in 310, and Adams is on the raft.
Germany: Haeckel's whispered avowal that substance is enigmatic. Mach rejects matter (Matter is Motion). They agree with Pearson that the supersensual is unknowable.
France: Poincare. Nature no longer loves simplicity; some approach to unity has been made; but the endless alternation of simple and complex turns the historian green.
Complexity has always been true. Poincare on mathematical continuity as symbols and on Euclid as convenient. The genealogy of Truth from Aquinas to Pearson.

The historian is a mere instrument of measure (keep a shortened version of the catalogue of ignorance). Motion and matter: 'we are probably incapable of discovering'. Radium as the next point since Zeno.
The historian must not seek truth. Thought moves like a cannon-ball: 310, 1500, Galileo and Bacon, then 1900 snaps. Balfour's dating.

The child of 1900 is born into a multiple world where order is artificial compulsion. It explains man's fiendishness, but the despotism of order lies ahead (the physicists' phrase). He wishes to escape.

The pearl-oyster image and woman's ordered universe. Lucretius' Venus, quoted in reduced form. 'Her supersensual chaos killed her.' Adams as a ball of vibrating motions at the feet of the Virgin or of Poincare. The mind cannot be satisfied: merge or succumb.

The Lucretius lines can be reduced to the first and fourth lines.
The fabulist 'frightened bird' paragraph can be condensed.
risks: Cutting Poincare's two contradictory quotations would lose the irony; both must stay together.
